application.purpose: Prioritize detected application identities across scoped hosts.

category_application.purpose: Separate application identities within each DetectRaptor category.

install_location.purpose: Measure normalized install locations for each application.

install_source.purpose: Measure normalized install sources for each application.

publisher.purpose: Measure publishers associated with each application.

event.semantics: event or artifact observation time

mtime.semantics: file, registry, or record modification time

selection.bias: Application detections show presence and install context, not necessarily malicious use.
selection.interpretation_caveat: Corroborate with host, path, signer, or execution evidence.
selection.preferred_use_case: Application inventory and suspicious tooling triage.

live_vql_select: if(condition=EventData.ScriptBlockText, then=EventData.ScriptBlockText, else=serialize(item=if(condition=Message, then=Message, else=EventData), format="json")) AS Evidence

detection.purpose: Low-noise triage by DetectRaptor detection name.

event.semantics: event or artifact observation time

selection.bias: DetectRaptor produces broad lead-finding results rather than case-specific proof.
selection.interpretation_caveat: Treat detections as leads requiring corroboration.
selection.preferred_use_case: Cross-host Windows lead-finding before narrower follow-up.

criticality_detection.purpose: Prioritize DetectRaptor MFT detections by configured criticality and detection identity.

detection_path.purpose: Separate normalized path variants within each DetectRaptor MFT detection.

string_hit.purpose: Measure exact filename or string variants matched by each MFT rule.

mtime.semantics: file, registry, or record modification time

selection.bias: DetectRaptor MFT is lead-oriented and can omit surrounding NTFS context.
selection.interpretation_caveat: Pivot to raw MFT or FileFinder for path and timeline precision.
selection.preferred_use_case: Lead-finding file and path triage.

rule.purpose: Prioritize PSReadLine matches by DetectRaptor rule identity.

command.purpose: Measure normalized PowerShell history command variants across hosts.

rule_command.purpose: Separate normalized command variants within each DetectRaptor PSReadLine rule.

mtime.semantics: file, registry, or record modification time

selection.bias: PSReadLine depends on retained per-user history.
selection.interpretation_caveat: Missing history is not evidence of no PowerShell use.
selection.preferred_use_case: PowerShell command-history lead review.

primary.purpose: Which downloaded paths and source URLs are unusual across the scoped hosts?

atime.semantics: host file SI last-access time; not Mark-of-the-Web creation or download time

btime.semantics: host file SI creation time; not a browser download timestamp

ctime.semantics: host file SI metadata-change time; not Mark-of-the-Web creation time

mtime.semantics: host file SI modification time; not a browser download timestamp

selection.bias: Coverage depends on surviving Zone.Identifier alternate data streams.
selection.interpretation_caveat: Absence does not disprove download or user access.
selection.preferred_use_case: Download and Mark-of-the-Web lead-finding.

category.purpose: Partition the large Autoruns inventory by persistence mechanism before any path or signer comparison.

selection.bias: Autoruns produces broad, mostly benign persistence inventory across common Windows autorun categories.
selection.interpretation_caveat: Category establishes persistence mechanism context; suspiciousness requires path, signer, launch-string, and hash review.
selection.preferred_use_case: Cross-host autorun and persistence review grouped first by Autoruns category.

primary.purpose: Which execution paths, SHA1 values, and program identifiers are rare across the scoped hosts?

mtime.semantics: file, registry, or record modification time

selection.bias: Coverage depends on available Amcache keys and parser support.
selection.interpretation_caveat: Strong execution/install support, but not complete coverage or always an exact execution time.
selection.preferred_use_case: Execution corroboration for known binaries or paths.

event.semantics: event or artifact observation time

mtime.semantics: file, registry, or record modification time

selection.bias: Native Amcache source variants expose different path, hash, and timestamp field names.
selection.interpretation_caveat: Amcache supports presence or execution hypotheses but does not prove a precise execution time by itself.
selection.preferred_use_case: Native Amcache contextual review after validating the connected-server schema.

event.semantics: event or artifact observation time

selection.bias: Very broad when IocRegex, channels, and EvtxGlob are not narrowed.
selection.interpretation_caveat: Use for bounded string or event hunts; broad fleet execution can overwhelm collection and review.
selection.preferred_use_case: Bounded IOC or adjacent-activity EVTX pivots using keyword-driven log-family selection.

primary.purpose: Which process-to-target-server pairs are unusual for explicit logons?

event.semantics: event or artifact observation time

selection.bias: Routine client-to-server authentication can dominate.
selection.interpretation_caveat: Review process and target context instead of treating every 4648 as suspicious.
selection.preferred_use_case: Credential-use and explicit-logon review.

event.semantics: Windows Event Log event time emitted by the public-IP detection

selection.interpretation_caveat: A public IP in an event record is a network lead, not proof of malicious activity.

primary.purpose: Which source-IP and event-id combinations are unusual for RDP authentication?

event.semantics: event or artifact observation time

selection.bias: Routine administrative and service authentication can dominate.
selection.interpretation_caveat: RDP-related rows do not by themselves prove malicious remote access.
selection.preferred_use_case: Focused remote-access review with source and time bounds.

primary.purpose: Which service names and normalized executable paths are unusual across the scoped hosts?

event.semantics: event or artifact observation time

selection.bias: Narrower than generic EVTX review but still depends on its command-line regex.
selection.interpretation_caveat: Absence does not disprove service creation through other paths.
selection.preferred_use_case: Service-install and ADMIN$-style follow-up.

primary.purpose: Which normalized executed-program paths are rare across users and hosts?

event.semantics: event or artifact observation time

mtime.semantics: file, registry, or record modification time

selection.bias: Only useful where BAM data exists and retention is limited.
selection.interpretation_caveat: Useful recent execution context, not historical completeness.
selection.preferred_use_case: Recent execution review on supported Windows systems.

primary.purpose: Which binaries and prefetch hashes are rare across the scoped hosts?

selection.bias: Server hosts often lack useful Prefetch by design.
selection.interpretation_caveat: Strong execution support where present; absence on servers is not unusual.
selection.preferred_use_case: Execution corroboration for desktop and workstation binaries.

primary.purpose: Which application identifiers are rare across the scoped hosts?

event.semantics: event or artifact observation time

selection.bias: SRUM can create large multi-scope outputs.
selection.interpretation_caveat: Use for usage windows and resource context, not exact execution moments.
selection.preferred_use_case: Timeframe and usage-pattern enrichment.

primary.purpose: Which filenames, extensions, and normalized paths are rare within the bounded timeline?

mtime.semantics: file, registry, or record modification time

selection.bias: Raw MFT is powerful but expensive; target the disk, filename, and path before fleet use.
selection.interpretation_caveat: Timestamp and filename evidence require surrounding context.
selection.preferred_use_case: Bounded adjacent-activity or file-presence pivots.

selection.bias: Usually low volume but can be empty depending on acquisition context.
selection.interpretation_caveat: Run on live systems; empty output is not universal proof of absence.
selection.preferred_use_case: Targeted WMI persistence follow-up.

primary.purpose: Which registry category, key, and value-name combinations are unusual across the scoped hosts?

mtime.semantics: file, registry, or record modification time

selection.bias: Registry Hunter is high-cost when multiple categories are collected; never select the all-category preset as routine scenario context or baseline evidence. IocRegex and Mtime bounds can substantially narrow an explicit use case.
selection.interpretation_caveat: Use an explicit category-scoped preset and interpret results within that registry use case. ModifiedAfter and ModifiedBefore bound registry-key Mtime, not execution time or value-level creation time. Verify the live artifact exposes these newer parameters before relying on them.
selection.preferred_use_case: Explicit category-scoped registry IOC/string search or Mtime-bounded timeline follow-up when the live artifact exposes IocRegex, ModifiedAfter, and ModifiedBefore.

primary.purpose: Which user-launched entries are rare across users and hosts?

selection.bias: Biased toward Explorer and GUI-driven user interaction.
selection.interpretation_caveat: Run count and focus metrics are not exact execution counters.
selection.preferred_use_case: GUI-based user-activity corroboration.

primary.purpose: Which filenames, normalized paths, and hashes are rare across the scoped hosts?

mtime.semantics: file, registry, or record modification time

selection.bias: Unbounded globs can expand rapidly across a fleet.
selection.interpretation_caveat: File presence is not execution evidence.
selection.preferred_use_case: Exact-path or tightly scoped IOC file pivots.

category.purpose: Partition the large Autoruns inventory by persistence mechanism before any path or signer comparison.

selection.bias: Autoruns produces broad, mostly benign persistence inventory across common Windows autorun categories.
selection.interpretation_caveat: Category establishes persistence mechanism context; suspiciousness requires path, signer, launch-string, and hash review.
selection.preferred_use_case: Cross-host autorun and persistence review grouped first by Autoruns category.

process_trust.purpose: Group running processes by image name, executable path, and Authenticode trust result so unsigned or untrusted binaries remain distinct from trusted binaries.

process_identity.purpose: Group running processes by the coherent process identity of image name, executable path, and complete command line.

selection.bias: A process-list snapshot favors long-running processes and can miss short-lived execution.
selection.interpretation_caveat: Process presence is not proof of malicious activity; review path, command line, user, signer, hash, and host prevalence together.
selection.preferred_use_case: Cross-host running-process prevalence and coherent process identity review.

dll_hash.purpose: Correlate identical service DLLs despite path or service-name changes.

executable_hash.purpose: Correlate identical service executables despite path or service-name changes.

executable_path.purpose: Find rare or non-standard service executable paths after path normalization.

failure_command.purpose: Surface recovery commands that can provide service-based persistence or execution.

name_path.purpose: Detect service-name path drift and masquerading across the fleet.

service_account.purpose: Identify unusual service logon accounts and fleet-level account prevalence.

service_dll.purpose: Separate svchost-backed services by normalized ServiceDll path.

service_name.purpose: Find rare, random-looking, or fleet-inconsistent service names.

start_mode.purpose: Establish the distribution of service start modes before filtering uncommon services.

selection.bias: Benign enterprise service volume can be high.
selection.interpretation_caveat: Service presence alone is not compromise; focus on path, account, start type, and change context.
selection.preferred_use_case: Service inventory and suspicious path/account review.

rmm_application.purpose: Prioritize installed RMM identities and observed display names.

selection.bias: LolRMM identifies dual-use remote management software that may be authorized or abused.
selection.interpretation_caveat: Authorization is host- and time-specific; installed presence is not proof of malicious use.
selection.preferred_use_case: Installed RMM inventory and authorization review.

selection.bias: Running RMM processes are dual-use and require authorization and command-line context.
selection.interpretation_caveat: A signed or common RMM process may still be unauthorized or abused. This profile has no declared process-start timestamp; treat it as a collection-time observation unless exact source context supplies a valid event time.
selection.preferred_use_case: Running RMM process and command-line review.

rmm_domain.purpose: Prioritize RMM identities and resolved domains.

selection.bias: DNS cache matches show name resolution, not necessarily execution or connection.
selection.interpretation_caveat: Corroborate DNS evidence with process, network, installation, and authorization context. This profile has no declared DNS-resolution timestamp; treat it as a collection-time observation unless exact source context supplies a valid event time.
selection.preferred_use_case: Resolved RMM domain review.

criticality_detection.purpose: Prioritize Amcache detections by criticality and identity.

detection_path.purpose: Measure path variants within each Amcache detection.

hash.purpose: Measure observed SHA-1 variants within each Amcache detection.

mtime.semantics: file, registry, or record modification time

selection.bias: Amcache detections show historical application metadata and may not prove execution.
selection.interpretation_caveat: Corroborate with Prefetch, process, event, file, signer, and timeline evidence.
selection.preferred_use_case: Historical suspicious binary and execution lead review.

rename_identity.purpose: Prioritize observed filenames that differ from PE original identity.

path.purpose: Measure path variants for renamed binaries.

hash.purpose: Measure hash variants for observed renamed filenames.

mtime.semantics: file, registry, or record modification time

selection.bias: Filename and PE-version mismatches can be legitimate packaging or deliberate masquerading.
selection.interpretation_caveat: Validate hash, signature, path, version metadata, and execution evidence.
selection.preferred_use_case: Renamed binary and masquerading lead review.

category_domain.purpose: Prioritize web-history categories and matched domains.

selection.bias: Domain intelligence matches can reflect research, redirects, legitimate services, or malicious activity.
selection.interpretation_caveat: Validate complete URL, user, browser artifact, time, download target, and correlated file or process evidence.
selection.preferred_use_case: Suspicious browser history and download lead review.

rule_process.purpose: Prioritize YARA process-memory rules and affected process names.

rule_path.purpose: Measure executable path variants for each process-memory rule.

selection.bias: YARA process-memory matches vary in quality and may include generic or overlapping signatures.
selection.interpretation_caveat: Validate rule metadata, matched context, process identity, path, signer, and corroborating evidence.
selection.preferred_use_case: Running malware and suspicious process-memory overview.

rule_path.purpose: Prioritize webshell YARA rules and target paths.

rule_tags.purpose: Measure YARA tag variants for webshell matches.

mtime.semantics: file, registry, or record modification time

selection.bias: Webshell YARA sets include rules with different specificity and may match benign application code.
selection.interpretation_caveat: Confirm web-root relevance, rule quality, file context, deployment state, and server activity.
selection.preferred_use_case: Webshell lead review over scoped web content.

path_version.purpose: Measure observed extension versions and source paths.

mtime.semantics: file, registry, or record modification time

selection.bias: Threat-intelligence extension matches show installed presence and may be stale or inactive.
selection.interpretation_caveat: Confirm browser/user scope, installation state, observed hash/version, metadata, and current enablement.
selection.preferred_use_case: Suspicious or malicious browser extension inventory review.

event.semantics: PowerShell script-block Event Log event creation time

selection.interpretation_caveat: EventTime records the script-block event, not script-file modification time.

event.semantics: service-creation Windows Event Log event time

selection.interpretation_caveat: EventTime is service event time; the artifact has no collection DateAfter or DateBefore parameters.

log.semantics: timestamp parsed from the AnyDesk trace log record

selection.interpretation_caveat: Timestamp is an AnyDesk log-record time, not installation or collection-observation time.

selection.interpretation_caveat: Analysis includes a session when either boundary is inside the incident window; collection-time bounds are artifact-owned and separate.

selection.interpretation_caveat: EventTime records the clear event, not the cleared log file modification time.

event.semantics: scheduled-task Windows Event Log event time

event.semantics: NTDSUTIL-related Windows Event Log event time

selection.interpretation_caveat: EventTime is available for analysis although the artifact exposes no collection DateAfter or DateBefore parameters.
The parent expands to Channels and Providers; each source uses registry-key Mtime rather than an Event Log event time.

mtime.semantics: event-channel registry key last-write time; not an Event Log event time

selection.interpretation_caveat: Mtime describes current registry state and does not prove when a specific channel setting changed.

mtime.semantics: event-provider registry key last-write time; not an Event Log event time

selection.interpretation_caveat: Mtime describes current registry state and does not prove when a specific provider value changed.

mtime.semantics: bootloader file modification time

selection.interpretation_caveat: File-system timestamps are not execution or compromise times and may be altered.
The wrapper has no safe shared time field; analysis resolves timestamp roles independently for each emitted source.

mtime.semantics: AppCompatCache control-set modification time; not a confirmed program execution time

selection.interpretation_caveat: ModificationTime describes cache state and must not be represented as execution time.

record.semantics: Amcache registry inventory record or key timestamp emitted by the source

selection.interpretation_caveat: Timestamp is Amcache record state, not proof of execution; InstallDate is excluded because observed formats were not consistently ISO timestamps.

execution.semantics: Windows Timeline activity last-modified time used as the source execution/activity timestamp

selection.interpretation_caveat: Timeline activity time is user-activity evidence and should be corroborated with process or file execution artifacts.
The source definition emits Bam_time, but IR9007 had no representative result row to validate the live result schema.
SRUM tables emit different TimeStamp, StartTime, and EndTime fields; IR9007 had no representative result row for this wrapper source.
Timestamp is parsed from an inventory identifier and observed values were empty or non-ISO; it is not enabled for server-side filtering.

execution.semantics: one Prefetch last-run timestamp emitted by the timeline source

mtime.semantics: Prefetch file modification time

selection.interpretation_caveat: event_time is execution evidence; prefetch_ctime and prefetch_mtime describe the Prefetch file.

mtime.semantics: RunMRU registry key last-write time emitted as event_time; not a confirmed command execution time

selection.interpretation_caveat: RunMRU key time indicates registry state and does not prove that a command executed at that time.
The source defines LastUsedTimeStart and LastUsedTimeStop, but IR9007 had no representative row to validate result shape and null handling.

selection.interpretation_caveat: EventTime records the compatibility-assistant event and should be correlated with other execution evidence.

execution.semantics: RecentApps last-accessed time emitted as LastExecution

selection.interpretation_caveat: RecentApps is historical registry state and LastExecution should be corroborated.
LastExecuted is a raw application-compatibility log string without a verified timezone; it is not enabled for server-side filtering.

selection.bias: Use as optional site-owned authentication context when the definition is installed.
selection.interpretation_caveat: Authentication records do not independently prove malicious access or downstream execution.
selection.preferred_use_case: Correlate Kerberos activity with exact accounts, systems, sessions, and other host evidence.

selection.bias: Use as optional site-owned logon context when the definition is installed.
selection.interpretation_caveat: A logon event must be interpreted using status, type, source, and surrounding evidence.
selection.preferred_use_case: Correlate logon activity with exact accounts, source systems, sessions, and event outcomes.

selection.bias: Use as optional site-owned NTLM context when the definition is installed.
selection.interpretation_caveat: NTLM activity does not independently establish credential theft, lateral movement, or compromise.
selection.preferred_use_case: Correlate NTLM activity with exact accounts, systems, addresses, and other authentication sources.

selection.bias: Use to complement script-block and command-history evidence when the site artifact is installed.
selection.interpretation_caveat: Module logging shows recorded PowerShell activity, not successful downstream effects.
selection.preferred_use_case: Review module and pipeline activity around a bounded PowerShell lead.

selection.bias: Use as an optional legacy execution trace when the source exists on the target.
selection.interpretation_caveat: RecentFileCache records are version dependent and should be corroborated with other execution sources.
selection.preferred_use_case: Corroborate a named executable or path using legacy application-compatibility state.

selection.bias: Use as a supporting execution-history source, not as a substitute for a deliberately bounded raw MFT and EVTX timeline.
selection.interpretation_caveat: Timeline rows combine sources with different timestamp semantics and require source-qualified interpretation.
selection.preferred_use_case: Corroborate execution and file activity across built-in forensic sources.

selection.bias: Collect early from a live endpoint because connection state is volatile.
selection.interpretation_caveat: A connection snapshot does not establish when a connection began, whether traffic succeeded, or whether it was malicious.
selection.preferred_use_case: Correlate current network tuples with process, user, DNS, and threat-intelligence context.

selection.bias: Use to complement the normal local-user inventory with hidden-account indicators.
selection.interpretation_caveat: A hidden-account indicator requires validation against account state and change evidence.
selection.preferred_use_case: Identify registry-backed local accounts that may be hidden from ordinary enumeration.

selection.bias: Use as supporting user and remote-resource context for lateral movement or staging questions.
selection.interpretation_caveat: Mount-point presence does not prove data access, transfer, or malicious use.
selection.preferred_use_case: Correlate remote shares and mounted resources with users, sessions, and file activity.

selection.bias: Use as the core local-account inventory for identity-state coverage.
selection.interpretation_caveat: Current account state does not establish when or by whom an account was created or changed.
selection.preferred_use_case: Establish local user identities and state before validating account-change hypotheses.

selection.bias: Collect early from a live endpoint as volatile user-session context.
selection.interpretation_caveat: A current session does not establish the original authentication path or malicious activity.
selection.preferred_use_case: Correlate active users with processes, connections, and authentication evidence.

selection.bias: Use as one persistence lane alongside services, tasks, WMI, and Autoruns.
selection.interpretation_caveat: A configured startup item does not prove execution or maliciousness.
selection.preferred_use_case: Inventory startup locations and corroborate suspicious entries with file and execution evidence.

selection.bias: Use as a supporting execution trace where the PCA source is available.
selection.interpretation_caveat: PCA records are not complete execution telemetry and require corroboration.
selection.preferred_use_case: Corroborate a named executable, path, or user with other execution-history sources.

selection.bias: Use as supporting boot-integrity context in defense-evasion review.
selection.interpretation_caveat: Boot configuration presence or variation is not independently evidence of tampering.
selection.preferred_use_case: Review bootloader and boot-configuration state around a concrete tampering hypothesis.

selection.bias: Collect early from a live endpoint because resolver-cache state is volatile.
selection.interpretation_caveat: A cached name does not prove a successful connection, user action, or malicious use.
selection.preferred_use_case: Correlate recently resolved names with live connections, processes, and other network evidence.

selection.bias: Use on live endpoints to establish current local administrator membership.
selection.interpretation_caveat: Current group membership does not establish when, how, or by whom the membership changed.
selection.preferred_use_case: Validate privileged local identities and select exact account-change follow-up.

selection.bias: Use as a core scheduled-task inventory in persistence-state coverage.
selection.interpretation_caveat: Task configuration does not independently prove execution, success, or maliciousness.
selection.preferred_use_case: Review task actions, principals, triggers, and related file or execution evidence.
